messages:
priya: Hey team — dropping the prototype for the routing policies editor. Want focused feedback on: rules builder UX, how we surface priority ordering, validation messages, and the preview simulator. https://figma.example.com/file/abcd1234

diego: quick skim — overall looks good. A few immediate things: the rule cards feel dense, hard to scan priority. Can we add a compact summary row and collapse details by default? :eyes:

ava: I agree with collapsing. Also we should show a visual priority indicator (numeric + small chevron to reorder). Drag handles are fine, but keyboard reordering is important for accessibility.

sam: noted. Today the list supports drag & drop only. Will add up/down buttons and aria-live announcements for reorder ops.

luisa: copy nits: the header currently says "Priority" but the tooltip explains "higher priority rules run first" which is inverted from some users' mental model. Maybe change label to "Order (runs top → bottom)" and tooltip: "Rules are evaluated top to bottom; first match applies."

priya: yes, explicit directional language helps. Also want clearer validation. Right now invalid rules show a tiny red dot — not discoverable. Suggest inline validation row with message and a contextual "Fix" button that opens the rule editor.

diego: +1. For conflicting rules we should surface a conflict badge at the top with an example of matched traffic — e.g., "2 requests/min would match rule X instead of rule Y". That ties to the preview sim.

ava: about the preview simulator: can we default to realistic samples (short user prompt, long system prompt) and let users toggle "sample traffic" sets? Also add toggle for "show matched rule" vs "simulate fallback".

sam: backend note — simulator will call the same routing logic but with synthetic inputs. Perf should be fine but need to cap runs per minute per workspace. ops-bot: rate limit set to 10 simulators/min for non-enterprise by default.

luisa: accessibility: contrast ratio on rule priority chip fails AA for disabled states. Use 3.5:1 min for disabled and 4.5:1 for active. Also ensure rule drag handles are >=44px touch target.

diego: validation messaging design: show three states — OK, Warning, Error. Error blocks saving; Warning allows save but shows a "Potential issues" toast with link to problem rules. Example warnings: overlapping catch-all with higher priority, or deprecated model used in rule.

priya: UX flow question: if a rule is invalid, do we allow toggling it off and saving? My vote: yes, allow save but persist invalid state and show inline badge so users can later fix.

ava: agree — but block rollout for Dedicated/private if there are Errors. Hosted can allow save with errors but warn about traffic loss.

sam: implementation detail — will expose an endpoint /preview?policyId=xxx returning a small simulation payload. We should design the UI to present a concise summary: matched_rule_id, reason, and simulated_response. Keep the raw JSON collapsible.

luisa: microcopy suggestion for the preview header: "Preview routing with example traffic" -> change to "Simulate how a request will be routed" (actionable).

priya: final checklist before we iterate in figma: 1) collapsed rule summary + expand; 2) reorder affordances (drag + keyboard); 3) three-tier validation UI + conflict banner; 4) preview simulator presets + show matched rule; 5) ARIA/contrast/touch targets; 6) copy tweaks for priority tooltip and preview header.

diego: I'll update the figma with the compact row and conflict banner.

sam: I'll add aria attributes and the up/down reorder controls in the branch (feat/routing-editor-reorder).

ava: can we add a tiny animation when rules reorder? helps perception but keep it subtle. 80ms fade + translate.

priya: love that. Also one more: validation message examples. Diego or Luisa, can you draft 2-line friendly error copy for: "conflicting rules" and "invalid model spec"?

diego: sure. Drafts: "Conflicting rules: this rule overlaps with a higher-priority rule and will never be reached. Consider changing order or narrowing conditions." and "Invalid model: the model spec used by this rule is deprecated or unavailable in the selected region. Select a supported model to enable this rule."

luisa: small tweak: make the first sentence shorter for scannability. My edit: "This rule is hidden by a higher-priority rule and will never run. Move it above the other rule or narrow the match conditions."

priya: perfect. Thanks all. Diego — once you push the updated frames, can we do a quick review Friday 10am?

diego: yep. Friday 10 works.

ava: will add an accessibility checklist to the figma file.

priya: great — if anyone spots any missing edge-case, add a thread reply here. Otherwise I'll close this once figma is updated. :white_check_mark:
